title: Renewal Failure Forensics Template
content:
Purpose: quick forensic template for investigating renewal failures (pre-QBR/after churn). Use this as the canonical working doc for a single-account deep dive. Focus: reasons + timeline + counterfactuals + prioritized mitigation actions.

Quick instructions (TL;DR):
- Fill top-level summary (executive) first — 2–3 bullets max.
- Populate timeline with hard timestamps (emails, support tickets, deployments).
- Map each loss reason to evidence and a plausible counterfactual (what we would have done differently).
- Add recommended owners and immediate next steps (outreach, product fixes, docs).
- Attach queries and raw artifacts as links.

Section A — Executive summary (to be used in QBR slides)
- One-line outcome: e.g., "Account X did not renew on 2026-02-28 — annual contract $120k — primary reason: sudden budget reprioritization + perceived latency regressions in production."
- 2–3 bullets: customer sentiment, primary product/eng issues, top recommended action (account rescue / product fix / enablement).

Section B — Basic account facts (fill from CRM)
- Account name:
- Region:
- ARR / Contract value:
- Contract term start / end:
- CS owner(s):
- Product leads engaged:
- Tier (self-serve / mid-market / enterprise):
- Last known usage (api calls / seats / monthly tokens):

Section C — Time-anchored timeline (required)
- Format: YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm — Event — Source (email/ticket/slack/call recording) — Link/ID
- Example entries:
  - 2025-11-12 09:34 — Initial POC signed up; Redwood API usage begins (trial) — CRM:lead-1782
  - 2025-12-03 15:21 — Support ticket #3421: "sporadic 503s during batch inference" — Zendesk #3421 (link)
  - 2026-01-15 11:00 — Quarterly check-in; customer mentions slow tail latency for long prompts — CS notes (link)
  - 2026-02-07 08:47 — Procurement pauses renewal pending TCO analysis — email thread (link)
  - 2026-02-24 16:10 — Renewal not approved; finance asks for discount — CRM opportunity lost (link)

Section D — Loss reason taxonomy (categorize, choose 1–3 primary)
- External / Customer-driven:
  - Fiscal/budget cut, org restructure, vendor consolidation
- Product-performance:
  - Latency regressions (tail latency), quality regressions, missing features (e.g., streaming, function calling), unreliable embeddings
- Commercial / pricing:
  - Price sensitivity, lack of flexible SKUs, unexpected egress/costs
- Adoption / enablement:
  - Low internal adoption, lack of integration, poor onboarding or docs
- Operational / trust:
  - Security/compliance gaps, audit concerns, unhappy with SLOs/support response

For each chosen reason include: Evidence (linked), Confidence (low/med/high), Primary owner (CS/PM/Eng/Sales).

Section E — Evidence map (must link artifacts)
- For each reason, list raw evidence: logs, Grafana snapshots, ticket transcripts, contract emails, POC metrics.
- Examples to attach:
  - grafana: api.p95 and p99 charts (link)
  - support: ticket export (text)
  - slack: #acct-x thread export (link, approximate timestamps)
  - call recording: 2026-01-15-x (link)

Section F — Counterfactual scenarios (this is the unique part — 3 columns)
- For each primary loss reason create 2–3 counterfactuals:
  - What we would have done differently (action)
  - When we would have done it (relative to actual timeline)
  - Expected impact on renewal (qualitative: likely/possible/unlikely)

  Example: Latency regressions
    - CF1: Proactively detect tail latency increase using model-aware latency alert rule and route traffic to faster variant (when: within 24h of first 503 spike) — Expected impact: likely improvement in renewal sentiment
    - CF2: Offer a temporary dedicated capacity trial for 30 days at reduced cost (when: after first production latency complaint) — Expected impact: possible

Section G — Root-cause analysis (technical + human)
- Root-cause worksheet (fill in short bullets):
  - Technical: what failed (e.g., batching misconfiguration, model variant mismatch, autoscaler bug)
  - Process: what signals were missed (e.g., no regression alert on eval; CS not looped into pager)
  - Commercial: pricing expectations vs. actual invoice surprise
- Note: cite exact PRs/tickets.

Section H — Immediate mitigation + 30/60/90 plan (prioritized)
- P0 (within 48h): Owner, action, rollback criteria, recipient list (who to email), template subject/body for outreach.
- P1 (30 days): Engineering fix or feature, CS playbook updates, QBR promise items.
- P2 (60–90 days): Product roadmap items, pricing SKU changes, onboarding improvements.

Section I — Outreach templates (copy/paste ready)
- Rescue email subject: "Follow-up — steps to address production latency and renewal"
- Body snippet: "Hi <name>, thanks again for the candid feedback. We investigated the 503s and identified... propose a short trial of dedicated capacity and a joint runbook to monitor p99 latency. Can we schedule 30–45 min to walk through options?"
- Executive escalation snippet: short bullet list for VP-level summary.

Section J — Data collection queries & artifacts (practical)
- Example SQL to pull usage trend (postgres):
  SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) as day, count(*) as calls, avg(latency_ms) as avg_ms, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) as p95_ms
  FROM api_requests
  WHERE account_id = '<ACCOUNT_ID>'
  GROUP BY 1
  ORDER BY 1 DESC

- Example Grafana panels to export: p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue length, instance CPU.
- Support ticket exports: include full text and CS triage notes.

Section K — Prioritization matrix (useful for orgs with limited capacity)
- Scoring columns: Impact (1–5), Confidence (1–5), Effort (1–5) — compute simple priority = Impact * Confidence / Effort.
- Example rows: dedicated-trial (I=4,C=3,E=2 => score 6), bug-fix-pipeline (I=5,C=4,E=5 => score 4).

Section L — Sample executive summary (copy for QBR deck)
- "Outcome: Account X declined renewal (−$120k ARR). Root causes: (1) budget reprioritization; (2) product performance regression impacting critical flows. Counterfactuals suggest a targeted dedicated-capacity trial combined with a fast p99 alerting rule could increase likelihood of renewal. Recommended next steps: run 30-day trial (owner: CS), ship priority latency fix (owner: Eng), update pricing FAQ and onboarding docs (owner: Product)."

Section M — Notes to self / open questions (keep informal)
- Who in Sales approved discount last year? Need to confirm margin thresholds.
- Should we treat budget reprioritization as a separate cadence for upsell attempts in 6–12 months?
- Is there a confluence page for "dedicated trial playbook"? If not, create one.

Appendix — artifacts checklist (tick when attached)
- [ ] CRM opportunity export
- [ ] Contract copy and terms
- [ ] Support ticket bundle
- [ ] Grafana snapshots (p50/p95/p99 + errors)
- [ ] Call recording and transcript
- [ ] Email thread showing procurement reasons
- [ ] Cost analysis (TCO) that procurement saw

Versioning: keep this doc as the canonical forensic for this account. If using a new doc per account, copy this file as "forensics-{account-name}.json" and update path.

Short log of changes (helpful):
- 2025-09-18 AP: initial draft scaffold
- 2025-11-21 LR: added SQL examples and prioritization matrix
- 2026-03-10 MB: added counterfactual examples, outreach templates

Unresolved: what metric threshold triggers a "rescue" outreach vs. "monitor and wait"? propose: p99>1000ms sustained for 48h OR error rate >1% for 24h. Open to debate.

END OF TEMPLATE — fill and attach evidence.
